To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

• the low-lying eigenvalues of the overlap kernel are very sensitive to the gauge field; • the overlap kernel can be made to have low-lying eigenvalue density close to zero, for a given gauge field, using the so-called “shifted” overlap kernel; • the low- lying eigenvalue density of the overlap kernel is very sensitive to the choice of gauge field;

1) the low-lying eigenvalues of the overlap kernel are sensitive to the choice of gauge fixing; 2) for a given gauge fixing, the low-lying overlap spectrum is insensitive to the gauge field itself, and is therefore independent of the dynamical configuration used to generate the overlap kernel; 3) for a given choice of gauge fixing, the overlap kernel can be approximated to high precision using a low-rank approximation; 4) for a given dynamical configuration,
the low-lying eigenvalues of the overlap kernel can be improved significantly by the addition of a random vector to the kernel, and by the addition of random vectors to the overlap operator.
